items.statement: Let $N=\prod_{i<k}p_i^{e_i}$, where $k\ge1$, the $p_i$ are distinct odd primes, and every $e_i\ge1$. If $z^2\equiv1\pmod N$ but $z\not\equiv1,-1\pmod N$, then both $\gcd(z-1,N)$ and $\gcd(z+1,N)$ are proper nontrivial divisors of $N$. When $k=1$, the hypotheses cannot hold, because the proof below shows the only roots are the two global signs.
